title: Why he took up music; teacher Shawnee
summary: No one in his family played; seeing a women's band at a theater made him want to play. Harold Dejan adds that the teacher charged 25 cents a lesson.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Uh-huh. And you said that nobody in your family played music before you?
Why did you, uh, you know, why did you want to take up music?
Well, it started on, uh, I saw a woman band at the, at the theater one day, and decided I wanted to take comfort from there. And I started taking that little man, Shawnee.
Uh-huh. Did he, uh, did he charge you for lessons, or, I mean, a regular teacher?
Oh, but I mean, a very small amount.
Oh, yeah. One of the best teachers they had to, he charged 25 cents a lesson.
And he wrote his own theory book for 25 cents. Gee whee. He did it for pleasure, for the New Orleans, uh, youngster to learn to play music. Uh-huh.
